analysis:
Reviewed the head text of SSDPrefixCache.swift (lines 657-1837). The only changed lines are 1794-1800, in retireIndexedEntries. The old code took removalLock once and removed all URLs in one critical section. The new code calls SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices(urls) and takes removalLock per slice. Each slice still checks hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot, so the root-safety and epoch-ownership guards are preserved on every slice. A nil return from a slice (closed cache, or epoch no longer current) is handled inside removeInSlices. The previous code returned an empty Result in that case, and the new code defers to removeInSlices to do the same. Its implementation was not supplied, so this contract is unverified. The call sites at 1779 and 1790 consume result.externalChange, indexedBytesFreed and removed, and externalChange still triggers reconcileExternalRemovals.

Security effect: a deletion batch is no longer atomic with respect to the removal lock. Concurrent donations, reads or purge operations can interleave between slices. That is probably a deliberate availability and fairness improvement, in line with T-060-style starvation concerns. The paths that honour the removal barrier are performIndexedRemoval, performExternalDestructiveChange and forgetMissing, which rechecks file status under the lock. They still serialize per slice. If a whole-root destructive change or epoch rotation happens between slices, the next slice re-evaluates ownsEvictionRoot, so stale deletes should not proceed.

The rest of the file is unchanged. It keeps HMAC-tag lookup, metadata binding (weightHash, layoutEpoch, lookupTag, window binding), authenticated streaming reads, and delete-on-corruption. No T-041 mitigation is weakened: no new plaintext metadata, no longer TTL, no change to the scope-salt handling.

Open question for integration: SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices (slice size, aggregation of removed/indexedBytesFreed/externalChange, early abort on nil) is outside the supplied evidence. Check that it aggregates results faithfully and that a nil slice stops further deletion rather than skipping the ownership check.
